findings.title: Backup-code authentication can bypass password verification
findings.body: The new backup-code branch accepts a valid backup code regardless of whether a supplied totpCode is valid. Earlier password verification is skipped whenever credentials.totpCode is nonempty. An attacker can therefore submit a valid backup code together with an arbitrary totpCode (for example, "x") and authenticate to a password-based account without knowing its password; the TOTP is never checked because the backup-code branch takes precedence. Ensure password verification cannot be bypassed by an unverified field when authenticating with a backup code.

findings.title: Consume backup codes atomically to enforce single use
findings.body: Backup-code verification reads the encrypted array and then overwrites it using an unconditional update by user ID. Two simultaneous login requests can read the same unused code, both validate it, and both successfully authenticate, violating the single-use guarantee. Concurrent requests using different codes can also overwrite each other's changes and restore a consumed code. Use an atomic compare-and-swap with retry or a suitably serialized transaction, and only authenticate after successfully consuming the code.
